chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: The missing critics
summary: Willard notes no critics wrote in the Chicago days, and Collins again wonders why he is excluded.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: Well, no, there weren't any critics during the Chicago days. then (inaudible)
The critics started later. But the thing is a lot of them have done some research, and somehow their research has skipped right over you.
I wish I knew how that could happen. I just don't know.
I don't think anyone was writing about jazz in those Chicago days, that I know of.
Well, I mean, they've mentioned everybody that was playing with me. I was playing with them. How
can they exclude me like this, this is what I don't understand.

You know, it's just amazing. Well, okay.
So any way, I've had the good fortune to have played with the giants, despite being, you know, ignored by the critics I was there, you know. And Basie and I, as I say we've been friends -- I met him around 1937, whenever they came to the Grand Terrace I met him. So we've been friends ever since.
